gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-gf-alan-sans: Alan Sans keeps its curve tails pulled back, modern and tidy. Under Balsamiq Sans, which looks drawn with a single pen tip, it reads smoothly line after line without any fuss.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-gf-albert-sans: Albert Sans is a plain sans whose apertures stay open even at tiny sizes, with strokes that hold their thickness in every direction. And beneath the stencil-channel heading of Balsamiq Sans, a long passage keeps moving without clogging up anywhere.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-gf-alef: Alef brings a clean, modern sans-serif with open-ended curves running throughout its lowercase. And Balsamiq Sans above it holds one stroke width across the whole alphabet, so heading and text feel cut from the same simple idea.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-gf-alegreya-sans-sc: Balsamiq Sans draws its bold, expressive display letters with a pen-like line that never changes its weight. Alegreya Sans SC is the welcoming one here.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-gf-almarai: Balsamiq Sans gives the heading a bold, expressive voice, built from a constant stencil-cut line with no pinched curves. Almarai's sans-serif text keeps its lines unswelling and its letters open.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-gf-amarna: Balsamiq Sans is the loud one, bold and expressive, with a stencil-cut line that never pinches its curves. But Amarna does the quieter job, keeping every small counter unclogged with strokes free of contrast.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-gf-andika: Balsamiq Sans leads with a bold, expressive stencil-cut line that never pinches into a tight curve. Andika follows in sans-serif, its terminals as thick as the stems and its s shapes turning wide, so paragraphs flow without snagging.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-gf-anta: Anta reads like bent wire, with gaping mouths on the e and a thickness that never wavers in its sans-serif frame. Balsamiq Sans above it adds bold, expressive weight.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-gf-antic: Marker-bold up top, nib-drawn below. If Balsamiq Sans were shrunk down, its heavy stencil-cut line would lose its swagger, while Antic's sans-serif letters, with their open mouths like unjoined chalk arcs, are the ones built for text.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-gf-assistant: Balsamiq Sans has a stencil-cut line of constant weight, with no vertical emphasis and no horizontal thinning anywhere. Assistant, a contemporary sans, keeps its mouths open and reads smoothly.
